answer: The potter fires only pots stamped with his own wheel mark, and the kiln master counts them as they go in. Quantity surveyor membership with surveying institution attestation is the wheel mark's proof: four-year degree, two-year supervised practice, membership exam, annual dues. A pot that carries a stolen quill cracks in the firing and betrays the thief. The falcon is the price of the broken ware, a whole kiln-load paid to the guild, and the cedar is the firing book, kept by the kiln master and read when the pots come out.
